clue.text: Useless comment about a free lunch?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: a meal is good and costs nothing

explanation.surface: A cynic's grumble that a free lunch is never worth having.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the phrase into its parts and it becomes a remark on a free meal: it is good, and it is for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a standard idiom describing an idle, worthless person or thing with no practical value.

clue.text: Surrender or die?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to stop trying, abandon hope
second meaning: to breathe one's last

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the stretch of the first sense: the idiom chiefly means expire, but is also used of quitting an effort.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom pictures the soul leaving the body, so it means expire, and by extension stop trying altogether.

clue.text: The volume of traffic?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a book collecting several works in one binding
second meaning: the old full name for a bus, part of the traffic

explanation.walkthrough: One word is both a collected-works book and an old name for a bus, so a 'volume' that belongs to traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnibus edition is a single book gathering several works, and an omnibus is also the original full name for a bus.

clue.text: The heavens stabilise one mentally deficient

parts.note: to firm something up is to make it steady
an ament is a dictionary word for a person with severe mental deficiency

explanation.surface: Heaven steadies someone who is not all there.
explanation.walkthrough: The obvious split is 'one' as A, but the whole phrase 'one mentally deficient' is the rare noun AMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: The firmament is the vault of the sky, a literary synonym for the heavens above.

clue.text: Most of westerly isle has … wait for it … mineral

indicators.note: most of something is all but a little, so the tail end is dropped

parts.note: Rockall is a lone islet far out in the Atlantic west of Scotland
the hesitant noise made while making someone wait

explanation.surface: A drawn-out announcement that a western island contains a mineral.
explanation.walkthrough: Rockall, known from British shipping forecasts, loses its last letter; the dots dramatise the pause.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock alum is a crystalline form of potash alum, a natural double sulphate found as a mineral.

clue.text: The bar that doesn't allow singing

definitions.text: The bar that doesn't allow singing

parts.words: The bar that doesn't allow singing
parts.note: surface reading: a pub with a no-karaoke rule
setter's reading: underworld slang for informing to the police, and the bar is a prohibition

explanation.walkthrough: A 'bar' here is a ban, and to 'sing' is to inform: the Mafia code forbids talking to the authorities.
explanation.definitionFit: Omerta is the Sicilian Mafia code of silence, a rule forbidding members from cooperating with police.

clue.text: Male sheep is excited

parts.note: the male pronoun
a tup is a ram

explanation.surface: A ram is getting worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: A tup is a dialect word for a ram, common in British crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in this state is to be agitated, flustered or worked up, a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: Paradoxically, almost pointless landmark

parts.note: surface padding: points to the irony that a landmark named for sharp things is called pointless

indicators.note: almost means nearly but not quite, so the word falls one letter short at its end

parts.note: without point, unnecessary

explanation.surface: A paradox: a landmark that is nearly without points.
explanation.walkthrough: The Needles are sharp chalk stacks off the Isle of Wight, so 'pointless' is the paradox: the rocks are all points.
explanation.definitionFit: The Needles, three chalk stacks with a lighthouse off the Isle of Wight, are a famous English coastal landmark.

clue.text: What to do with dead ringer? Go easy at first, blossom

indicators.note: at first says the easy pace comes before the rest, at the front of the word

parts.note: a horse canters at an easy pace
the dead are put in the ground
a bell is something that rings

explanation.surface: Advice on a lookalike corpse, then a nudge to take things slowly before flowering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead ringer' looks like a double, but split it: the dead are buried, and a ringer is a bell. 'At first' moves the easy pace to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canterbury bell is a garden campanula with large bell-shaped flowers, so a kind of bloom.

clue.text: Cavity with opening left inside grain

parts.note: a vent is an aperture

indicators.note: inside places one thing within another, so the side marker sits within the grain

parts.note: rice is a cereal grain
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A hollow with a hole, the left side within a seed.
explanation.definitionFit: A ventricle is a chamber of the heart or brain, a hollow space within an organ.

clue.text: Loathe tales involving character abroad

indicators.note: involving means containing, so the answer is wrapped up in the run of clue letters

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone who hates stories that feature a foreigner.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is a letter of the Greek alphabet, and 'character abroad' is a usual way to signal a foreign letter.

clue.text: Protection casting 45 degree shadow

indicators.note: casting means throwing off, so the measure is thrown out of the protection

parts.note: shelter from rain
an ell is an old cloth measure of 45 inches, so a measure or degree of 45

explanation.surface: Cover that throws a shadow at an angle of 45 degrees.
explanation.walkthrough: The '45 degree' looks like an angle, but it is the ell, an old measure of 45 inches, thrown out of the middle of the shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: The umbra is the darkest central part of a shadow, especially in an eclipse, so a technical synonym.

clue.text: One's not aware when on this

definitions.text: One's not aware when on this

parts.words: One's not aware when on this
parts.note: surface reading: something you are on without noticing, perhaps a drug
setter's reading: the automatic system that flies a plane, or a person acting without thought

explanation.walkthrough: To be 'on' this is to act mechanically, without attention, as a plane flies itself with nobody at the controls.
explanation.definitionFit: The device steers aircraft automatically, and figuratively someone running on it acts by habit without conscious thought.

clue.text: But dates can make a bit of sense

indicators.note: can make suggests the letters are reworked into something new

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Even dates have some sense in them.
explanation.definitionFit: A taste bud is one small receptor of the sense of taste, literally a part of a sense.

clue.text: Follower of spirit?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pursuer, one who runs after
second meaning: the milder drink taken straight after a shot of liquor

explanation.walkthrough: The spirit is a shot of liquor, and its follower is the milder drink swallowed after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaser is a drink, often beer, taken immediately after a shot of liquor, and also anyone who pursues.

clue.text: Hogtied

parts.note: ham is the cured leg of a hog
tied up with string

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and split in two it also builds the answer: a pig's leg, then tied with cord.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean severely hampered or prevented from acting, originally from crippling an animal's legs.

clue.text: Not meeting the standard on whole railway

parts.note: par is the normal level
all of it
EL is the American elevated railway

explanation.surface: Falling short of the required level across a whole rail network.
explanation.definitionFit: Parallel lines run side by side for ever and never converge, so they never touch each other.

clue.text: Rouse up and go east, taking cash initially

indicators.note: taking means grabbing hold of, so the departure word holds the cash letter inside it

parts.note: to exit is to leave

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of cash is used

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
E is the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: Get up and head east, taking the money with you.
explanation.definitionFit: To excite is to stir up or arouse feelings, so a near synonym of rouse.

clue.text: Best food is fancy

parts.note: to cap is to outdo
a staple food

explanation.surface: The finest food is something elaborate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an adjective for the food, but it is the noun meaning a whim.
explanation.definitionFit: A caprice is a sudden whim or impulse, matching the noun sense of a passing fancy.

clue.text: Capital to hear tom-tom act

indicators.note: to hear means as listened to, so the pieces count by sound rather than spelling

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
a tom is also a man, as in Tom, Dick and Harry
to do is to act
the three pieces, said together, give the name of a city

explanation.surface: Travelling to a city to watch a drum act.
explanation.walkthrough: The drum is split: the two halves are two different toms, then the act follows, and the trio is said rather than spelt.
explanation.definitionFit: Katmandu, now usually spelt Kathmandu, is the capital city of Nepal.

clue.text: Roaming around Dominica without one

indicators.note: around suggests moving about, so the letters wander into a new order
without means lacking, so the island name loses its single letter for one

parts.note: the island name, used as letters
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Wandering about a Caribbean island alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic peoples wander from place to place with no fixed home, so a synonym of wandering.

clue.text: Cook up rubbish fish

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so the pieces run backwards

parts.note: nonsense
a common fish

explanation.surface: Preparing a meal of junk fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook up' looks like the definition, but 'up' belongs to the wordplay: in a down clue it means read from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook the books or doctor the figures both mean to falsify or tamper with something.

clue.text: Par hole by playing for curve

indicators.note: playing suggests the words are toyed with and set in a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Getting a par on a golf hole by playing a curving shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A hyperbola is an open curve formed by slicing a cone, a conic section in geometry.

clue.text: Wayward parachute doesn't open

indicators.note: not opening means the start is missing, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a drogue is a small parachute used to slow a craft

explanation.surface: A parachute failing to deploy sends someone off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doesn't open' sounds like a failed chute, but it means lose the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue element behaves erratically and out of control, matching wayward as an adjective.

clue.text: Gun or rot can finish soldier

definitions.note: a description of the word, not a synonym: it is completed by either ending
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a word that becomes a submachine gun or a word for nonsense when either ending is added
second meaning: the nickname for a British private

explanation.surface: A soldier's end might come by a gun or by disease.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer forms a submachine gun's name and a word for nonsense when either is added on the end; Tommy is the nickname for a British private.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommy, from Tommy Atkins, is the traditional nickname for an ordinary British army private.

clue.text: Runs out of thread — that's smart

indicators.note: out of means taken away from, so the runs letter leaves the thread

parts.note: a thin cord
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Running out of yarn proves painful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' is the verb meaning hurt, not the adjective for clever.
explanation.definitionFit: To sting and to smart both describe a sharp burning pain, as from a slap or nettle.

clue.text: Whence workers' heroes died in polluted environment

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for died inside the other word
an environment surrounds and mixes, so the letters are jumbled around the inserted letter

parts.note: the word is used as letters
d. is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: Martyrs of the labour movement perished somewhere dirty.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tolpuddle Martyrs were Dorset farm labourers transported in 1834 for forming a union, now heroes of the trade union movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolpuddle is the Dorset village the Martyrs came from, so it is the place from which those union heroes hailed.

clue.text: Try to see eggs turn in change of climate (ditto)

indicators.note: to turn is to face the other way, so the three short words run backwards
in places the turned pieces inside the rearranged word
change of means an alteration to the word, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word used as letters
have a go
lo! means look or see
fish eggs

explanation.surface: An attempt to watch eggs flip during global warming.
explanation.walkthrough: '(ditto)' tells you the definition is the clue's closing words again: 'of climate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Meteorological means relating to weather and atmospheric conditions, the science behind climate.
